incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into Rosstat's IT systems disrupted the agency's ability to publish data; a Belarusian opposition hacktivist collective claimed responsibility.
incidents.impact: Russia's statistics agency failed to publish scheduled weekly price data and other economic reports, with delays expected to continue through at least Nov. 13, and some previously published data disappeared from the agency's website.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack, attributed by Italian officials to pro-Russian hackers, compromised government communications tied to the foreign minister's office.
incidents.impact: Confidential information concerning Italian government officials was reportedly offered for sale online; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni linked the incident to a rise in hybrid disruptions from Russia-aligned actors.

incidents.victim: Multiple companies in financial services, healthcare, and other sectors
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud using AI deepfakes
incidents.vector: Three men used AI-generated voice and video deepfakes to impersonate company CEOs and law-firm attorneys, directing accounting staff to wire funds for purported confidential transactions.
incidents.impact: The scheme defrauded at least $129 million from victims including a UK fintech, a Florida pet-food company, hospital systems, a mutual fund company, and a bank between July 2024 and February 2026; three defendants were arrested and indicted in the U.S.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the internal network of Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the method of entry was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Data on 3,600 ministry employees, including names and email addresses, was stolen in an intrusion that took place at the end of July; the ministry says the secure portion of its network was not affected.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Norad's network via 27 compromised accounts.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to more than 20,000 grant applicants was stolen; Norad is working with Norway's National Security Authority to investigate.

incidents.vector: An attacker used what the company described as 'offensive agentic techniques' combined with an on-path interception attack to compromise internal tools and capture passwords in transit.
incidents.impact: Names, usernames, password hashes, and active authentication tokens for all Chainalysis users — including law enforcement, national security, and crypto-industry customers — were exposed, and some customer accounts on its transaction-monitoring service were accessed.

incidents.victim: Mobile users in Ukraine, the U.S., and Europe
incidents.vector: The group compromised legitimate websites and a Ukrainian web-analytics vendor to inject device-fingerprinting code, then delivered exploit chains against unpatched iOS and Android devices.
incidents.impact: Thousands of iPhone and Android users were exposed to data-theft malware capable of harvesting messages, credentials, call logs, contacts, and photos; most victims were in Ukraine, with others in the U.S. and Europe.

incidents.vector: A ransomware gang encrypted library systems; the initial access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: On-site computers, checkout machines, Wi-Fi, digital media services, and the library's mobile app were taken down across the 66-branch system serving 2.3 million Queens residents; no gang has yet claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: A former FBI counterintelligence agent used his authorized access to FBI systems holding seized cryptocurrency credentials to conduct roughly 100 fraudulent transfers across 35 separate investigations.
incidents.impact: The agent stole approximately $2.47 million in cryptocurrency from seized wallets tied to criminal and nation-state investigations, compromising multiple FBI cases; he pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering and faces up to 20 years.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House)
incidents.vector: White House staff devices had residential-proxy apps installed via bundled SDKs in free mobile and desktop software, one tied to a Russian-linked company, which rent out device bandwidth and IP addresses to third parties.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed 236 proxy exit events from the White House's dedicated network over roughly a month via at least 28 different residential-proxy services, exposing the network to potential abuse by unknown third-party renters.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into the French banking group's systems enabled theft of funds, later traced through on-chain laundering.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole $133 million from the French banking group; blockchain investigators identified the theft after the stolen funds were moved for laundering.

incidents.victim: A Ukrainian manufacturing company in the transportation sector
incidents.vector: Belarusian government-linked hackers deployed destructive wiper malware against the target's systems, per a security researcher's Q2-Q3 2026 threat-activity report.
incidents.impact: The attack destroyed data on systems at a company with an important role in Ukraine's transportation sector, marking the group's first confirmed destructive data-wiping operation.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers took over master user accounts on Li Auto smart EVs — most registered with Chinese eSIMs provided by importers — to lock owners out of their vehicles.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed Li Auto owners in Russia had their vehicles hijacked and were extorted to regain control; the actual number of affected vehicles is believed to be higher.

incidents.victim: Owners of Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices worldwide
incidents.attacker: China — commercial device manufacturer, financially motivated
incidents.vector: A Chinese device manufacturer allegedly built backdoor malware into Android TV boxes that enrolled devices into a botnet and sold access to residential-proxy resellers and other criminal affiliates.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million Android TV boxes were infected and used for ad fraud and bandwidth resale; Google and industry partners dismantled the botnet's infrastructure, which also risked exposing an additional 10 million connected IoT devices.

incidents.victim: Supermarket chains and blood banks across Europe
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited internet-exposed refrigeration controllers with weak or default credentials to force units into continuous defrost and heating cycles.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of supermarkets across France and at least 10 other European countries suffered spoiled food and equipment damage, including an estimated €250 million loss at one retailer; refrigeration at three French blood banks was also targeted, though no plasma was lost. Pro-Russian hacktivist groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed credit.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access was detected within the company's IT network, prompting a temporary suspension of testing operations and order management systems.
incidents.impact: Myriad Genetics is investigating whether patient records were accessed; most systems have returned to normal operation and the company does not currently believe the incident will be material.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency platforms including Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance, and Origami Finance
incidents.vector: An attacker compromised a customer support account at domain registrar Name.com and used it to redirect at least 15 cryptocurrency-related domains to phishing sites.
incidents.impact: Customer wallets connected through the hijacked domains were drained; the hijacks took place on October 31.

incidents.vector: Russian-linked hackers breached the Ukrainian news outlet's content management system.
incidents.impact: The attackers sent a fraudulent newsletter containing false claims that President Zelensky had been shot and that he had launched a nuclear weapon against Kyiv.

incidents.vector: Attackers used a fake job-interview social-engineering scheme and a compromised Homebrew installer to plant malware on Binance engineers' machines, then used an internal AI tool to pivot to wallet-infrastructure engineers and steal signing access.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen in the largest crypto theft on record; about $2.8 billion was later frozen, leaving over $3.25 billion unrecoverable. The FBI attributed the theft to a North Korean hacking group it tracks as TraderTraitor.

incidents.vector: A hacktivist group claims it obtained the data from a DHS Okta-based identity system; Okta denies any compromise of its own systems.
incidents.impact: Records for roughly 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including ICE, CBP, USCIS, and CISA personnel — names, emails, phone numbers, reporting structures, and over 55,000 internal permissions groups — were published by transparency group DDoSecrets.

incidents.victim: Financial sector organizations in Southeast Asia and globally
incidents.vector: The actor used an agentic AI offensive framework combined with conventional tools to scan for and exploit flaws such as server-side request forgery and anonymous file upload, deploying open-source remote-access trojans for persistence.
incidents.impact: Compromised financial organizations faced automated credential brute-forcing, lateral movement, and data exfiltration conducted at machine speed with reduced need for hands-on-keyboard activity.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations with cloud and GitHub-hosted code
incidents.vector: Threat actors used agentic AI tooling to mass-search public GitHub repositories for exposed secrets and application credentials, then used compromised OAuth and service-principal credentials to access Microsoft Entra ID tenants and Azure resources.
incidents.impact: In one case an AI agent progressed from searching GitHub for leaked secrets to exfiltrating data from an organization's Azure Key Vault in five minutes; affected organizations saw cloud resource enumeration, credential theft, and abuse of AI service API keys.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached government IT systems and began extracting data before being detected by government IT staff.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly a third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach, in one of the country's worst cybersecurity incidents to date.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime, and global shipping companies
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware and data extortion
incidents.vector: The group compromised a maritime IT services provider and pivoted from that single access point into dozens of its port authority and shipping-company customers.
incidents.impact: More than 40 maritime and port organizations were listed on the group's dark web leak site after a payment deadline expired on Oct. 19; roughly half of the victims are known customers of the same IT services provider.

incidents.vector: An internal business system was inadvertently moved out of a VPN-restricted network during a migration, leaving it externally accessible and allowing an unauthorized account to access a customer database.
incidents.impact: Customer names, business emails, phone numbers, and identity documents such as driver's licenses and passports were exposed; DigiCert says certificate-issuance capability and login credentials were not affected.
